outcome.answer: Raven directly targets long-context recall in linear-time sequence models. It uses input-dependent routing to update selected memory slots, aiming to reduce interference from dense state updates and avoid the hard eviction of sliding-window attention; the paper reports strong recall on benchmarks and effectiveness at contexts up to 16 times its training length [1]. Kaczmarz Linear Attention instead adjusts residual-write step sizes in a linear recurrence, reporting improved associative recall and stability up to 65K tokens [2]. Adaptive Memory Decay takes a log-linear approach, learning content-dependent memory decay and reporting gains on long-range recall tasks [3].
